questions.question: During logic synthesis and physical design optimization, how is Multi-Threshold CMOS (Multi-Vt) library cell swapping primarily utilized to balance power and performance?
options: Low-Vt (LVT) cells are placed on timing-critical paths to reduce delay, while High-Vt (HVT) cells are used on non-critical paths to minimize subthreshold leakage.
High-Vt (HVT) cells are placed on timing-critical paths to boost drive strength, while Low-Vt (LVT) cells are used on non-critical paths to reduce dynamic switching power.
Low-Vt (LVT) cells are used exclusively in sequential elements (registers), while High-Vt (HVT) cells are strictly reserved for combinational logic.
High-Vt (HVT) cells are assigned to lower metal layers, while Low-Vt (LVT) cells are routed only to top-level global interconnects.
Ultra-Low-Vt (ULVT) cells are used during functional testing modes to increase noise margins, then swapped to High-Vt during normal operation.

questions.question: According to Amdahl's Law, what fundamentally limits the theoretical maximum speedup achievable by parallelizing a computing workload across an arbitrarily large number of processor cores?
options: The physical propagation delay of electrical signals through the interconnect network
The proportion of the program's execution time that is inherently sequential (non-parallelizable)
The memory bus bandwidth available to feed cache lines into individual cores
The power delivery network's ability to maintain nominal supply voltage under peak current loads
The overhead incurred by hardware-managed cache coherence protocols like MESI

questions.question: In digital circuits, when an asynchronous signal violates the setup or hold time requirements of a flip-flop, the internal storage node may enter an unstable state with an output voltage lingering between valid logic levels for an unpredictable duration. What is this phenomenon called?
options: Ground bounce
Subthreshold leakage
Metastability
Negative-bias temperature instability (NBTI)
Thermal runaway

questions.question: In modern superscalar processor front-ends, what is the primary operational distinction between a Branch Target Buffer (BTB) and a conditional branch direction predictor?
options: The BTB resolves data hazards in the pipeline, whereas the branch direction predictor handles control hazards.
The BTB predicts whether an indirect jump will succeed, whereas the branch predictor manages function call-return addresses.
The BTB operates exclusively during the instruction execution stage, whereas the branch predictor operates during instruction fetch.
The BTB predicts the target instruction address before instruction decoding, whereas the direction predictor determines whether a conditional branch will be taken or not taken.
The BTB translates virtual branch addresses into physical addresses, whereas the direction predictor counts dynamic branch frequency.

questions.question: In modern high-performance microprocessors, what is the primary role of Miss Status Holding Registers (MSHRs) within a non-blocking cache?
options: To maintain least-recently-used (LRU) metadata for eviction candidate selection
To stage speculative dirty write-backs until instruction commit in the Reorder Buffer
To track cache line invalidation requests arriving from peer cores in a directory-based protocol
To buffer instructions fetched during a branch misprediction penalty cycle
To track outstanding cache misses so the cache can continue serving subsequent hits or independent misses
